questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Different country and different culture, also a good quality of study for my major.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Amazing international exchange, I got so many friends from different countries which largely broaden my horizons.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, Boston University has a special teacher to guide us for everything.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received many assistance from the professors because I cannot registered in the courses I want because those courses are restricted to the students enrolled in Bioinformatics Program in BU, but I successfully enrolled with the help of the professors, so if you are worried about picking the courses, don't worry, just wait and ask the professor after arriving!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Everything is good, you can get to know everything when attending the orientation.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Double room in a school dorm or in a hotel called Hyatt Regency Cambridge.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We have to buy meal plans for the entire semester as this is one of the requirements if you want to stay in a dorm.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You may be assigned to a hotel called Hyatt Regency which is very good! And be prepared to live with someone else as your roommate, most of the time your roommate will also be an exchange student.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was assigned into a hotel, which is very good, we have room service and 24 hours gym and free shuttle to the campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not that easy because some courses is restricted to the students enrolled in some specified program, you need to contact the professor to ask them to get you enrolled after the semester starts.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You will have a MyBU account and you can register yourself through that account, sometimes the course is full, then you will need to join in a waitlist to get yourself enrolled.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All the professors in BU are very willing to help, don't be afraid to ask!

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my courses I want.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you cannot registered in the courses you want, don't be panic, just ask in person after the semester begins, the professors are always willing to help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not that difficult and I have learned some contents before, but there are also new things to learn which is good.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level of the courses are easier than UCPH, some courses encourage more academic thinking that real academic knowledges.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More discussion session and also more chances to do projects on your own.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Omics Fundamentals, Bioinformatics Foundations and Institutional Racism in Health and Science.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Omics Fundamentals, can learn more about the combination of biochemistry and bioinformatics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really, all the fees are reasonable.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Housing and insurance are more expensive than expected, food is less expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They have so many different clubs to join which is very fun.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds, from fencing to dancing to even mahjong are available.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I like mahjong haha, in which you can meet many people and also have fun!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go and travel around US during the holiday, from Texas to Florida, from New York to Washington DC, you won't regret it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I met many friends from Singapore, I really like hang out with them which made my exchange life way easier and happier.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just ask and chat with them, the local students are always very friendly.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Sometimes they are more prefer to play with their little groups.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Good combination of different races regardless of skin colours and heritages.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Make some friends and don't be shy!
2. Remember to take this chance to travel across the US.
3. Treasure every experience that you may get.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Boston is a very safe and good place to live in, don't be afraid of security problems and also the winter there can be way colder than Copenhagen.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Friends from all over the world and we are still in contact from time to time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Try to find a way to not to pay tips lollll, to be honest, everything goes well, I really like this exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Not really :)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
